steps.description: The devotee takes four simple, even steps forward (R-L-R-L), hands in Pataka (showing direction of travel or general attention), representing the journey towards the temple.
steps.rasa_expression: A calm, slightly softened facial expression (Sama Drishthi) suggesting focus on the destination.
steps.teaching_note: Focus on maintaining the Araimandi consistently while walking; keep the steps simple and on the heel-flat-foot.

steps.description: Stops the forward movement and slowly raises both hands in Alapadma up to chest level, representing the first sight or dawning awareness of the deity.
steps.rasa_expression: A slow, widening of the eyes and a slightly parted mouth (Visamaya) conveying awe and realization.
steps.teaching_note: The hand movement should be gentle and upward; the body should remain grounded and still.

steps.description: Hands transition from Alapadma to Katakamukha and are brought close to the chest, preparing for the final offering/prayer.
steps.rasa_expression: Gaze is fixed on the invisible deity ahead; a faint, tender droop of the lips conveying gentle devotion/pity (light Karuna).
steps.teaching_note: Ensure the Katakamukha mudra is held cleanly and centered; the transition should be slow and deliberate.

steps.description: The hands are joined together in Anjali Mudra (formed by bringing the two Pataka mudras together) and held up in a position of prayer (Pranamya) for four beats.
steps.rasa_expression: Head bows slightly (Adhomukha) in reverence; the expression is one of humble and heartfelt devotion (light Karuna).
steps.teaching_note: The Anjali mudra should be held above the chest, near the chin; focus on maintaining stillness and stability throughout the four-beat hold.
